_provenance.policy: Every band below carries the URL it came from and the date it was verified. Where the source publishes no desktop/mobile split, the band says so explicitly instead of carrying an invented number.
_provenance.mobile: Core Web Vitals good/poor boundaries (web.dev) — these are FIELD boundaries at the 75th percentile; the gate applies them to a single lab run as a build-time proxy.
_provenance.desktop: Lighthouse publishes its own, stricter LAB thresholds for desktop on the per-audit Chrome for Developers pages (LCP, FCP, TBT). CWV itself does NOT split by device — where Lighthouse publishes no desktop number (CLS, INP) the mobile boundary is reused as a conservative proxy and labelled as such.

lcp_ms.note: CWV: good ≤ 2.5s, poor > 4.0s. Same numbers on the Lighthouse mobile audit page.

tbt_ms.note: Not a Core Web Vital — Lighthouse lab metric, mobile bands green 0–200ms / orange 200–600ms / red > 600ms. It is the lab proxy for INP, which cannot be measured here.

fcp_ms.note: Lighthouse mobile bands green 0–1.8s / orange 1.8–3s / red > 3s; identical to the web.dev FCP boundaries.

inp_ms.note: FIELD-ONLY here. CWV: good ≤ 200ms, poor > 500ms. A Lighthouse navigation run performs no interactions, so it emits no INP value — these bands are recorded for CrUX/RUM comparison and are deliberately NOT scored by the gate (measured:false). Lab proxy = tbt_ms.

lcp_ms.note: Lighthouse desktop bands green 0–1.2s / orange 1.2–2.4s / red > 2.4s. Stricter than the 2.5s/4s CWV boundary because Lighthouse desktop is a faster lab profile.

cls.note: No official desktop split; using the mobile boundary as a conservative proxy. Lighthouse publishes no desktop-specific CLS bands and CWV states the same thresholds apply to both device classes.

tbt_ms.note: Lighthouse desktop bands green 0–150ms / orange 150–350ms / red > 350ms.

fcp_ms.note: Lighthouse desktop bands green 0–0.9s / orange 0.9–1.6s / red > 1.6s.

inp_ms.note: FIELD-ONLY here — see the mobile entry. No official desktop split; CWV publishes one pair of boundaries for both device classes.

reference._note: Sourced boundaries the gate does NOT enforce. Recorded so a field/CrUX read can be judged against the same numbers the gate uses, without silently adding a new blocker.

ttfb_ms.note: Not a Core Web Vital (diagnostic for LCP). Good ≤ 0.8s, poor > 1.8s. No official desktop split. Not enforced: on a Shopify-hosted storefront TTFB is dominated by Shopify's edge, not by anything the theme controls.
